# Domain reference: Finance

Job family covered: Accountant, Management Controller, Administrative and Financial Manager (RAF), CFO (DAF), Treasurer, Credit Manager.

---

## Core competencies (x3)

| Competency | Junior / Accountant | Experienced / Controller | Senior / RAF | Leadership / CFO (DAF) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Accounting & financial technical mastery | Data entry, account matching (lettrage), bank reconciliations, routine tax filings. | Period-end closings, consolidation, reporting, variance analysis. | Supervises accounting production, manages the budget, builds forecasts. | Defines the financial strategy, engages with the statutory auditors (commissaires aux comptes), manages cash. |
| Financial analysis & management | Produces reliable financial statements. | Builds dashboards, analyzes margins, identifies drifts. | Manages the forecast, challenges operational teams on their figures. | Arbitrates investments, manages the P&L, presents to the board. |
| Compliance & standards | Applies accounting standards (PCG, the French chart of accounts, or IFRS depending on context). | Ensures tax and payroll compliance, prepares audits. | Manages relations with the tax authorities and auditors. | Defines the compliance policy, anticipates regulatory changes. |

## Secondary competencies (x2)

| Competency | Junior | Experienced | Senior | Leadership |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tools & systems | Masters the accounting software (Sage, Cegid, etc.). | ERP configuration, workflow automation. | Leads finance tooling transformation projects. | Defines the finance IT strategy, selects solutions. |
| Financial communication | Produces clear statements. | Explains the figures to operational teams. | Presents to executives, makes financial issues accessible. | Communicates with investors, bankers, the board. |

## Complementary competencies (x1)

| Competency | Description |
|---|---|
| Operational collaboration | Works with the business teams to make data reliable and understand variances. |
| Cash management | Cash forecasting, flow management, banking relationships. |
| Business / tax law | Understands the tax and legal implications of transactions. |

---

## Recommended role-play scenarios

- **Variance analysis**: present a monthly report with significant variances on 2-3 items. Ask the candidate to identify the probable causes, the questions to ask operational teams and the corrective actions. Observe: analytical rigor, ability to distinguish signal from noise, pragmatism.
- **CODIR presentation**: ask the candidate to present fictional financial results to a non-financial audience. Observe: clarity, ability to make things accessible, ability to bring out the key messages without drowning them in numbers. (CODIR = comité de direction, executive committee.)

## Red flags

### Red
- Accounting logic errors on basic topics (confusing expenses and fixed assets, not understanding the balance sheet)
- Unable to explain the figures they produce
- No reference to compliance or standards in their practice

### Orange
- Exclusive focus on production with no analytical vision
- Difficulty stepping back from detail to give an overview
- No curiosity about the business behind the numbers
